description: Weekly plan for ages two to six: love of prayer through example, tantrums, sleep, screens, fears and sibling jealousy.

topics.focus: Loving prayer through example, not orders

actions.text: Pray in front of them and invite them to stand beside you if they like, with no pressure.
Give them a small prayer mat of their own to place next to yours.
Praise any attempt — standing, a prostration, copying you — and leave the corrections for later.
Twice this week at bedtime, talk with them in simple words about the blessings Allah has given them.
When they get angry, get down to their level and name the feeling: "You're angry because the toy was taken."
Stay close and calm until the storm passes, and save the talk about behaviour for afterwards.
Offer two acceptable choices instead of a direct order: "The blue one or the red one?"
Notice when the tantrums happen this week; hunger and tiredness are among the most common triggers.

topics.focus: Regular sleep and a calm routine

actions.text: Keep the same bedtime every night, weekends included.
Switch screens off an hour before bed and replace them with a story or a quiet talk.
Follow the same order each night: bath, teeth, bedtime adhkar, a story, lights out.
If they get up at night, walk them back to bed calmly and with few words, every time.
Agree on a short, fixed screen time each day and give a five-minute warning before it ends.
Watch with them instead of leaving them alone, and talk about what you saw.
Make meals and bedrooms screen-free for the whole family.
Keep alternatives within reach: blocks, crayons and picture books.
Listen to the fear without teasing: "I understand you're scared of the dark."
Approach what scares them together, gradually and in small steps, never by force.
Leave a dim light on in their room if they are afraid at night.
Teach them to say "Bismillah" and breathe slowly when they feel afraid.

topics.focus: Sibling jealousy: every child gets their share

actions.text: Give each child ten minutes a day alone with you.
Avoid comparing siblings in front of them, even to encourage.
Name the jealousy calmly: "You feel upset when I hold your brother."
Let them help care for the younger sibling with small tasks, and praise the help.

topics.focus: Special time that strengthens the bond

actions.text: Play for ten minutes a day at a game they choose, without directing it.
Read a picture book together at bedtime and ask them about the pictures.
Hug them and tell them you love them for no reason, once every day.
At the end of the day, ask: "What was the best thing that happened today?"

worship.text: Pray Maghrib together at home once this week and invite the children to stand with you.
Recite the short surahs together at bedtime on three nights this week.
Say "Bismillah" before meals and "Alhamdulillah" after, out loud, so the children copy you.
Put a small charity box at home and let your child drop the coins in with their own hand.
Visit a relative together this week with the intention of keeping family ties.
